prompt:
This part belongs to the Vertical Cloud Lab "Powder Doser" — an auger-fed,
screw-metered dry-powder dispenser. Design it as a single, manifold,
FDM-printable solid (0.4 mm nozzle, ~0.2 mm layers; fin/wall features >= 2 mm).
All dimensions are in millimetres.

Shared fits & fasteners (apply where relevant):
- M3 clearance hole = 3.4 mm dia; M3 self-tap pilot = 2.7 mm; M3 setscrew pilot = 2.5 mm.
- M5 clearance hole = 5.4 mm dia.
- Auger / collar / bracket running fit over the 25.0 mm auger OD = bore 25.5 mm.
- Printed gears: module given per part, 20 deg pressure angle.

BASEPLATE — the fixed ground reference that the mounting plate hinges on and
that carries the two tilt servos.

Flat rectangular forward tab in the XY plane, thickness 6.0: X from -100 to
+100 (200 wide), Y from +55 to +115 (60 deep). The two rear corners (the
Y=+115 edge, at X=-100 and X=+100) are chamfered 25.0 x 45 degrees. Four M5
clearance holes (5.4 mm) for mounting at X = +/-80, Y = +68 and Y = +105
(clear of the chamfers). The plate's bottom face sits at Z = -14 (top face at
Z = -8); model it as a flat slab with the four holes and the two chamfers.

design_plan.description: Baseplate for Powder Doser - fixed ground reference with flat rectangular forward tab, chamfered rear corners, and four M5 mounting holes
design_plan.notes: Model as flat slab from Z=-14 to Z=-8. Apply 45-degree chamfers at rear corners (Y=115 edge) at X=-100 and X=+100, cutting 25mm along both X and Y edges. Four M5 clearance holes at (±80, 68) and (±80, 105). Ensure minimum wall thickness of 2mm maintained around holes. The chamfers remove triangular sections from the rear corners.

checks.message: All constraints met. The baseplate geometry is correct: bounding box spans X from -100 to +100 (200mm wide), Y from 55 to 115 (60mm deep), Z from -14 to -8 (6mm thick) — all matching specifications exactly. The rendered views confirm: (1) The flat rectangular plate shape is visible with appropriate proportions. (2) Both rear corners at Y=+115 show 45-degree chamfers cutting 25mm along each edge, creating the angled corners visible in all three views. (3) Four M5 clearance holes (5.4mm diameter) are clearly visible in the high-angle rear view, positioned at the correct locations X=±80, Y=68 and Y=105 — well clear of the chamfered corners. The volume of ~67,700 mm³ is physically plausible for a 200×60×6mm plate minus two triangular chamfer cuts (each removing ~1,875 mm³) and four small holes. The code correctly constructs the plate as a box, applies boolean cuts for the corner chamfers, and drills through-holes at the specified coordinates.
